content.title: Does Death Make Us Think?
content.subtitle: We must prepare before time runs out.
content.body:
Many people who stood beside us in the mosque last Friday are no longer alive today. Death happens around us every day. Some die in road accidents; others lose their lives in building collapses or earthquakes. Sometimes, we spend the night talking happily with a friend, only to wake up the next morning and hear that they are gone.

We have witnessed countless times that death is certain, but its timing is unknown. Yet how do we react? We may feel sad for a day or two after hearing about someone's death. Then we return to our old ways. We fall back into bad habits, secret sins, and neglect our prayers and worship. We forget that our name could be next in this procession of death.

We Will Be Resurrected in the State We Die

Have we ever thought about this? If the Angel of Death takes our soul right now, we will be raised before Allah on the Day of Judgment in the very state we die.

The Prophet ﷺ warned us: "Every person will be resurrected in the state in which they died." (Sahih Muslim: 2878)

Think about standing before the Almighty Allah, whom we have never seen, but whose fear and pleasure inspire believers to pray at night, give charity, and stay away from sin. What if we are raised while committing sins, in an impure state, or with no good deeds to show? How will we face Him with such shame?

Death Is Not a Cinematic Scene

Movies and dramas have led many of us to imagine death as something peaceful and romantic, as if we simply close our eyes and everything ends without pain. But reality is very different. The pain of the soul leaving the body, known as Sakaratul Maut, is beyond what any living person can imagine.

  • The Prophet’s ﷺ Final Moments: Aisha (RA) narrated that during the Prophet’s ﷺ final moments, there was a container of water beside him. He repeatedly dipped his hand into it and wiped his face, saying: "There is no god but Allah. Surely, death has its agonies!" (Sahih al-Bukhari: 4449)

  • Amr ibn al-As (RA): On his deathbed, his son asked him what death felt like. He replied: "My son, it feels as if the heavens and the earth are pressing down on me, and my soul is being pulled out through the eye of a needle!" (Siyar A'lam al-Nubala: 3/77)

  • Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA): Even Satan would avoid the path taken by Umar (RA). Yet, when he remembered death and the accountability of the Hereafter, he would pick up a piece of straw and say: "I wish I were this piece of straw! I wish my mother had never given birth to me!" (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 35563)

If those who were promised Paradise feared death so deeply, what should we, burdened with sins, feel?

How Should We Prepare for Death?

Many of us think preparing for death means doing a few good deeds one day out of sudden emotion. But it does not work that way. Preparing for death is not a one-day decision. It is a lifelong effort.

The Prophet ﷺ said that the truly wise are those who remember death often and prepare well for what comes after it. (Ibn Majah: 4259)

The key to this preparation is to reduce our attachment to worldly life and endless desires. The attractions of this world often keep us distracted from the Hereafter. That is why the Prophet ﷺ instructed us to remember death often, as it takes away worldly pleasures. (Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2307) This helps us control our desires and live like travellers passing through this world. (Sahih al-Bukhari: 6416) May Allah grant us all a life and death filled with faith.
